title: Worksheet 6: Booleans (V2.0)
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: A boolean is a data type that can only hold one of two possible values: true or false. Booleans are named after George Boole, a mathematician who developed a system of logic based on true and false values in the 1800s, long before modern computers existed. In programming, booleans are especially useful for making decisions, since a program can check whether a boolean value is true or false and then choose which instructions to run based on the result. For example, a video game might use a boolean variable called "isGameOver" to keep track of whether the game has ended, starting the value as false and changing it to true only once a specific condition, such as a player running out of lives, has been met. Booleans are often the direct result of a comparison, such as checking whether one number is greater than another, since a comparison like this can only ever be true or false, never anything in between.

questions.text: According to the paragraph, a boolean can hold:
questions.correct: Only the values true or false
distractors: One value of any data type

questions.text: According to the paragraph, who were booleans named after?
distractors: The inventor of the first computer
The company that built the first calculator

questions.text: According to the paragraph, what are booleans especially useful for in programming?
questions.correct: Making decisions about which instructions to run
distractors: Storing long messages for the user
Sorting numbers from smallest to largest

questions.text: A game uses a boolean called "isGameOver" that starts as false. Based on the paragraph, when would it change to true?
questions.correct: Once a specific condition is met, such as the player running out of lives
distractors: As soon as the game is opened
Every time the player scores a point
Never, because booleans cannot be changed

questions.text: A program checks whether 8 is greater than 3. Based on the paragraph, what kind of value does this comparison produce?
questions.correct: A boolean, because a comparison can only be true or false
distractors: An integer, because both values are numbers
A string, because it is written out in words
A float, because the answer needs precision
